## The opportunity

[Coding agents are one of the largest token workloads. DW's async tier is **20–28% cheaper**, but nobody uses it interactively.]{.lead}

| per M tokens | Realtime | Async |
|---|---:|---:|
| Kimi K3 · input / output | $3.00 / $15.00 | **$2.15 / $11.25** |
| DeepSeek V4.1 Flash · input / output | $0.15 / $0.60 | **$0.12 / $0.48** |

: {tbl-colwidths="[50,25,25]"}

::: {.fragment}
**The question:** can a harness make the slow, cheap tier feel realtime?
:::

## Evidence base: 78 runs on one real task

[**p-map** is a popular JavaScript library for running async work in parallel. The task: add a cancellation feature to it, with tests, types and docs.]{.lead .small-lead}

## What Fanout is

```{=html}
<div class="tiers top">
 <span><i class="sw t1"></i><b>Tier 1</b> realtime LLM · the interactive part</span>
 <span><i class="sw t2"></i><b>Tier 2</b> cheap LLM · async-eligible</span>
 <span><i class="sw td"></i><b>Deterministic</b> code · no LLM calls</span>
</div>
<div class="arch">
 <div class="stage fragment" data-fragment-index="0">
  <span class="eyebrow">1 · Plan</span>
  <div class="box rt"><span class="tier t1">Tier 1 · realtime LLM</span><b>Planner</b></div>
  <div class="box det"><span class="tier td">Deterministic</span><b>Compiler</b><small>contracts + dependency graph</small></div>
  <p>A fast model scopes the task. Code turns the plan into bounded work units, each with owned files and checks.</p>
 </div>
 <div class="stage fragment" data-fragment-index="1">
  <span class="eyebrow">2 · Execute in parallel</span>
  <div class="lanes">
   <div class="lane"><div class="box t2"><span class="tier t2">Tier 2 · cheap LLM</span><b>Worker A</b><small>own worktree</small></div></div>
   <div class="lane"><div class="box t2"><span class="tier t2">Tier 2 · cheap LLM</span><b>Worker B</b><small>own worktree</small></div></div>
   <div class="lane dep"><span class="wait">after A</span><div class="box t2"><span class="tier t2">Tier 2 · cheap LLM</span><b>Worker C</b><small>own worktree</small></div></div>
  </div>
  <p>Each worker edits only its own files in its own worktree, so parallel work never conflicts. Tier 2 can run on async.</p>
 </div>
 <div class="stage fragment" data-fragment-index="2">
  <span class="eyebrow">3 · Integrate</span>
  <div class="box det"><span class="tier td">Deterministic</span><b>Validate</b><small>checks per unit</small></div>
  <div class="box det"><span class="tier td">Deterministic</span><b>Integrate</b><small>bounded repair</small></div>
  <div class="box det"><span class="tier td">Deterministic</span><b>Final gates</b><small>full test suite</small></div>
  <p>Every result is checked before it's accepted. Failed work gets a bounded repair, never an open loop.</p>
 </div>
</div>
```

# A product idea for Doubleword {.center-title}

## An agent-session tier

```{=html}
<div class="tiercards">
 <div class="tcard">
  <span class="eyebrow">Realtime</span>
  <dl><dt>First request</dt><dd>starts now</dd><dt>Follow-ups</dt><dd>start now</dd><dt>Price</dt><dd>full</dd><dt>Fits</dt><dd>chat, IDEs</dd></dl>
 </div>
 <div class="tcard new">
  <span class="eyebrow">Agent session · new</span>
  <dl><dt>First request</dt><dd>queues like async (~60s)</dd><dt>Follow-ups</dt><dd><strong>fast</strong>, within a bounded session group</dd><dt>Price</dt><dd>async entry + continuation premium</dd><dt>Cache</dt><dd>kept warm for the session</dd><dt>Fits</dt><dd>coding agents, parallel harnesses</dd></dl>
 </div>
 <div class="tcard">
  <span class="eyebrow">Async</span>
  <dl><dt>First request</dt><dd>queues (&lt;1 min)</dd><dt>Follow-ups</dt><dd>queue again, every time</dd><dt>Price</dt><dd>~25% cheaper</dd><dt>Fits</dt><dd>background jobs</dd></dl>
 </div>
</div>
<div class="apisketch"><span class="eyebrow">API sketch</span><code>service_tier: "agent" · session: { id, max_group: 10, idle_timeout: "90s" }</code></div>
```

::: {.notes}
The gap in the tier lineup: agents are interactive but tolerate one upfront wait. Bounded groups and idle timeouts let DW schedule capacity; under load, a session can fall back to plain async.
:::

## Does the agent tier pay off?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
| Continuation price | Raw Pi · DW models | Fanout · DW models |
|---|---:|---:|
| Async rate | $0.63 | $0.31 |
| Midpoint "agent" rate | $0.74 | $0.31 |
| Full realtime rate | $0.84 | **$0.32** |

: {tbl-colwidths="[44,28,28]"}

::: {.caption}
Cost per task on p-map, modeled from the R2 and F2 traces. First request of each group of 10 at async rates; cache preserved. Time with groups of 10: Fanout 10.7 min vs 27.7 min on plain async.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="45%" .payoff}
- **For users of a parallel harness, the premium barely matters:** workers are cheap and the planner is realtime anyway. Fanout stays **42% cheaper than raw Sol** even at full realtime rates.
- **For a single-agent loop, a full premium erases the saving**, so the tier pairs best with parallel harnesses.
- **For DW, the premium pays for held capacity and a warm cache**, while group size, idle timeouts and a fallback to plain async keep scheduling bounded.
:::
::::

# Deep dives {.center-title}

## What we measured (all realtime)

{{< include charts/measured.md >}}

::: {.key}
[<i class="k-measured"></i>measured]{} · dashed line = raw Sol · one clean run per setup · all four passed independent acceptance
:::

::: {.fragment}
Same DW models, one run each: Fanout took **8.7 vs 11.5 min** at **63% lower cost** than raw Pi. Against raw Sol, Fanout cut cost but not time; p-map has little parallel work.
:::

## Where the money goes

{{< include charts/split.md >}}

::: {.fragment}
- The Kimi **planner is 85%** of the F2 cost.
- All DeepSeek implementation work: **$0.047**
- Each extra unit of work costs **~$0.04**, vs ~$0.19 on Terra. Parallel work costs pennies.
- What if the planner ran on a DeepSeek-priced model? **$0.31 → $0.05** (no quality evidence yet).
:::

## Where Fanout wins: tasks with parallel parts

{{< include charts/width.md >}}

::: {.caption}
Modeled: equal units, concurrency 4, fixed realtime planner, unit taken from the F2 critical worker (19 requests). p-map itself is narrow (~1–2 parts).
:::

::: {.notes}
Async on every request never wins on time, even at infinite width: 19 serial waits per worker. With groups of 10 it wins from 4 parts: 0.59× time, 0.19× cost.
:::

## Reliable small models

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="64%"}
{{< include charts/reliability.md >}}
:::
::: {.column width="36%"}
Repairs **eat the time margin, not the cost margin.**

::: {.fragment}
Measured:

- Raw Kimi: 2 of 3 passed, one hit the 20-min timeout
- One DeepSeek worker timed out at 10 min
:::
:::
::::

::: {.caption}
DeepSeek async + groups of 10, 4 parallel parts, relative to raw Sol. One repair re-runs a unit on the critical path.
:::

## What's holding it back {.autolist}

::: {}
1. **Verbose open-weight output.** 4–6× the output tokens of Sol/Terra; one Kimi response ran 25k tokens over 7.5 min.
2. **Mistakes are expensive.** Timeouts and repairs sit on the critical path.
3. **The planner dominates cost.** It must stay realtime, so it has to get cheaper or less verbose.
4. **Long request chains.** Every request in a row pays the async wait.
:::

## Ideas for Doubleword {.autolist}

| Idea | Why · evidence |
|---|---|
| **Agent-session tier:** async entry, bounded fast continuations (group size, idle timeout), priced as a premium | async Fanout 27.7 → 10.7 min; Fanout stays at $0.32 even at realtime continuation prices |
| **Session cache affinity:** route queued and continuation requests to warm replicas; report cache hits on async | raw Kimi async: $0.63 warm vs $1.50 cold |
| **Critical-path hints:** let a harness mark which request others are waiting on, and schedule parallel siblings with shared prefixes together | Fanout's critical worker is 19 requests deep; its sibling is 3 |
| **Async progress and deadlines:** queued → running → first-token events, queue ETA, server-side deadlines | poll-only today; *measured:* 10- and 20-min timeouts in our runs |
| **Agent-tool integrations with conformance tests** in CI against new tool versions | *measured:* a Pi update dropped the system prompt and tools, which looked like a Kimi failure |

: {tbl-colwidths="[55,45]"}

::: {.caption}
Evidence is modeled unless marked measured.
:::

## Appendix · method and caveats

- **Active time** = planning + execution; excludes dry runs, confirmation or operator waits, setup.
- **Cost** = token-price estimates. Sol/Terra from Pi's model catalog; DW from the snapshot retrieved 2026-09-20.
- **Async:** +60s per affected request, generation unchanged. Planner always realtime.
- **Continuations:** hypothetical. First request of each group pays +60s, at async prices.
- **Concise output:** output tokens and post-first-token time scaled.
- **Width model:** synchronized waves, equal units, from one narrow task.
- **Runs:** about 120 live runs across 5 tasks, 78 of them on p-map (evidence slide). The walk uses one representative clean run per setup; the evidence slide shows the spread.
